newsitem.title: INDIA: Tribal rebels ambush security patrol, kill 18.
newsitem.headline: Tribal rebels ambush security patrol, kill 18.

text.p: Separatist tribal guerrillas on Wednesday ambushed a security patrol in northeastern India and shot dead 17 paramilitary soldiers and a policeman, state police said.

"A group of National Liberation Front of Tripura militants this morning ambushed a Central Reserve Police Force patrol party and killed 17 CRPF personnel and a state policeman," police superintendent Bibhuti Chaudhury told Reuters in the capital of Tripura state, Agartala.
Three paramilitary soldiers were critically wounded in the attack, which occurred in southern Tripura's Natunbazar area at 8:30 a.m. (0300 GMT). The NLFT is an outlawed guerrilla group.
The Tripura government has asked the army and paramilitary troops to launch a search operation for the insurgents, Chaudhury said.
State Home (Interior) Minister Samar Chaudhury later told reporters: "The government will take stern action against all the insurgent outfits."

A separate group of tribal guerrillas in February killed at least 50 people in west Tripura, setting houses ablaze and leaving thousands homeless. The federal government later issued shoot-at-sight orders to army troops deployed in the area.
